source.repro: The last 400 non-merge commits on main as of b5c18e35ac; the 264 that touched a .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx source file still present, test files excluded. Each suite is priced at the median of its durations in jest's perf cache (node_modules/.cache/jest/perf-cache-jbrowse-default-*), footprints are the primary checkout's from one full run, and per commit each strategy's selected suites are summed. 'static' is @jest/core SearchSource.findRelatedTests over the commit's files in one process. 'footprint' selects suites whose footprint holds a changed file after dropping files whose @babel/preset-typescript output (comments: false, compact) is identical at C^ and C. 'no web' drops products/jbrowse-web suites unless the commit touched a jbrowse-web source file.
source.notes: Graph and footprints are today's while the commits are historical, so a file's importers are today's rather than the commit's. 'footprint, no web' selected no more suite-seconds than 'static, no web' on any of the 264 commits; a footprint is a subset of the static graph apart from one suite over the whole set, and the compile filter only removes. About 40% of commits touch a module every app-level suite executes at import (a config schema, a plugin index, render-core's marks), which is what keeps the with-web mean high. Function-level selection off V8 precise coverage was measured and declined: it added ~27% to every run and moved the with-web mean by ~6%, because most changed lines in those modules are top-level.
